data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible pairs of leaflets attached at the same node along the rachis in all images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaflets are closely spaced along the rachis, forming a compact leaf structure)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3.	Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaf is clearly divided into multiple distinct leaflets attached to a central axis/rachis)
    4.	Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): even-pinnate (leaflets are arranged in pairs along the rachis without a terminal leaflet at the tip in all visible views)
    5.	Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 6 (three pairs of leaflets are clearly visible on the primary rachis)
    6.	Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (leaflets are arranged in pairs at each node along the rachis)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7.	Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins appear smooth and continuous without teeth, though some margins have irregular holes)
    8.	Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are widest near the middle and taper towards both ends)
    9.	Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10.	Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf base appears broadly curved without a distinct taper or heart shape)
    11.	Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single central midrib with secondary veins branching off to the sides)
    12.	Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, spaced, numerous (secondary veins curve upwards towards the margin and are distinct on the leaf surface)
    13.	Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny, rugose (surface reflects light indicating a waxy cuticle and has a textured, raised appearance due to venation)
    14.	Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15.	Petiole length (short / long): short (the leaflets attach very close to the rachis, indicating a lack of a distinct petiole or a very short one)
    16.	Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): N/A (petioles are not distinct enough to assess features)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17.	Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears rigid, brown, and lignified)
    18.	Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19.	Stem color: brown (visible on the thin rachis and stem segments)
    20.	Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (stem appears relatively smooth without obvious ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21.	Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at the leaf bases or nodes)
    22.	Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23.	Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint-like structure visible at the leaf base)
    24.	Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)
F. Notes: The leaflets show distinct damage characterized by holes and missing sections along the margins. The venation is impressed on the upper surface, giving the leaf a rugose texture.
